correctness.rationale: A pentagon vertex interior tangent cone has opening 3π/5; five evenly spaced inward bisectors at angular gaps 2π/5 imply a real planar direction illuminates at most two cyclically adjacent vertices and every adjacent pair is attainable with strict inequalities. Product tangent cones factor, so every product direction is contained in one of exactly 25 cyclic 2×2 tiles; this is a theorem about ALL real directions, not a finite-direction assumption. Each of five rows of the 5×5 vertex grid needs three covering tiles, while every tile intersects two rows: 2N≥15 gives N≥8. Independently checked the specified 8 tiles cover all 25 cells with exact row multiplicities and are realizable. Every vertex is contained in four tiles, so uniform weight 1/4 on all 25 achieves fractional 25/4; dual vertex summation 25≤4W gives optimality. Vertex illumination implies boundary illumination via active facet inclusion. Exact geometry plus combinatorial certificates prove all pentagon side lengths; finite tile checks alone would not prove the geometry.
residual_risks: Only two equiangular pentagon factors; arbitrary products remain open.
An older cyclic-grid tile-cover theorem could duplicate the eight-cover combinatorics, although geometry reduction still needs argument.
